Wedding Venue Deposit Scam UK: Verify Before Paying

Confirm the booking and bank details through the venue’s independently found contact information before sending a deposit or balance.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-06-09 · Updated 2026-07-10 · 3 min read

wedding venue scamwedding deposit fraudfake wedding bookingvenue deposit scam UKwedding venue impersonation
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Report it — call Report Fraud on 0300 123 2040 (Police Scotland: 101), and forward scam texts to 7726.

Two different problems can look similar

A criminal may invent a venue or impersonate a real one and collect a deposit for a booking that does not exist. Alternatively, a real booking may exist but a criminal intercepts or imitates an email and substitutes new bank details. The latter is payment-diversion or invoice fraud.

A genuine venue that later cancels, fails to provide the service or becomes insolvent is a consumer or supplier-failure problem, not automatically fraud. Recovery routes can differ.

Warning signs

  • A late or unexpected change to bank details.
  • Pressure to pay urgently to keep the date.
  • Contact details that differ from the venue’s independently found site or earlier records.
  • Refusal to allow a visit or verified phone conversation.
  • A contract, invoice or business identity that cannot be reconciled with the venue.

Verify the request

Call the venue using a number you found independently or used before the payment change. Do not use a number, link or reply address in the new invoice. The National Crime Agency advises checking changed invoice and bank details by calling the genuine supplier on a previously used number because email can be intercepted or diverted.

Confirm the legal contracting party, venue address, date, services, cancellation terms and payment schedule in writing. A Companies House record can help check a limited company’s identity, but it does not prove the information filed is accurate and it will not cover every sole trader or business structure.

Deposits and cancellation terms

The CMA has warned wedding venues that large non-refundable deposits and disproportionate cancellation charges can be unfair. That is separate from fraud: a legitimate venue can still use an unfair term, and the precise consumer remedy depends on the contract and circumstances.

Payment protection

For a qualifying credit-card purchase, section 75 may apply where the cash price of the service is more than £100 and not more than £30,000. Paying only the deposit by credit card can still engage section 75 for the whole qualifying purchase, but the debtor-creditor-supplier relationship and other legal conditions must exist.

Chargeback may be available for card payments under scheme rules, commonly with a time limit around 120 days. It is not a statutory guarantee.

If a fraudster tricked you into a UK Faster Payment or CHAPS payment on or after 7 October 2024, the APP reimbursement rules may apply, normally up to £85,000, subject to scope and exceptions. A genuine commercial dispute with a real venue is not automatically an APP scam claim.

If you already paid

Contact the bank or card issuer immediately and explain whether this was an impersonation, fake venue, changed bank detail or supplier dispute. Ask the bank to contact the receiving bank if it was a transfer. Notify the genuine venue through verified details and preserve the contract, invoice, messages and payment record.

Report fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland; in Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101. Citizens Advice’s consumer helpline is 0808 223 1133.

Frequently asked questions

Does section 75 always cover a wedding deposit?

No. It can apply when the qualifying cash price and credit relationship are present, even if only a deposit was put on the credit card. The issuer must assess the facts.

Are changed bank details proof of fraud?

Not proof, but they are a strong reason to stop and verify through a previously used or independently found contact.

Does a Companies House listing prove the venue is genuine?

No. Companies House performs basic filing checks and warns that registration does not mean it has verified or validated the information.

Fast checks

  • Pause before sending money or credentials
  • Verify with an official site, app, or number
  • Never share one-time passcodes
  • Be sceptical of bank transfer pressure
